title: The Little Cookie Thief
markdown:
Once, in a little house with moon flowers, lived Cherry, a soft little chinchilla, and Wren, a woolly lamb. Cherry was so soft, like a little cloud on the window. Her fur was like soft dust. Wren was woolly, the woolliest lamb. Her wool was warm like the sun. She smelled like happy flowers and soft air. They watched the world from their window. The day said goodbye. The sky turned soft colours, like sleepy purple.

On their window, where the moonlight played, sat special cookies. They were shaped like little moons, round and small. They had a little honey and a sprinkle of sparkle. These moon cookies were perfect for a little bite before sleep, a sweet treat. Cherry and Wren loved these cookies so much. But tonight, they looked, and something was funny.

“Oh my,” Cherry whispered. Her whiskers wiggled. “My moon cookie is… smaller.”

Wren looked with her gentle eyes. “Mine too,” she said softly. A little bit was gone from Wren’s cookie. Cherry saw a little bite mark on hers.

They watched quietly. The moon climbed up. It peeked over the sleepy hills. Outside, little bugs sang sleepy songs. A soft breeze moved the flowers. Cherry settled down. Her soft fur touched the cool wood. She felt so calm. Wren snuggled close. Her wool was so warm, like a fuzzy hug.

They waited. They watched. Their eyes were wide, looking in the soft shiny light. No loud noises. No surprises. Just quiet. The night was peaceful.

“Hmm,” Cherry wondered. Her little nose wiggled. “Who is it?”

Wren made a soft sound. It was like a happy sigh.

Then the moon made a shiny line on the floor. They saw it. A tiny nose. Tiny whiskers. Two little paws reached out from the sill. It was a little mouse. Very small. Its fur was brown like dry leaves.

The mouse ate the last bit of Wren’s cookie. It looked up with big dark eyes that sparkled. Its eyes looked sorry. They seemed to say, Oh dear. I was so hungry. The moonlight shone on its tiny ears. They looked like flower petals.

Cherry felt soft inside, like a warm hug. Wren nodded slowly. She understood. The mouse looked so hungry. Maybe its tummy was rumbling. It looked sorry for eating their cookies.

Cherry pushed her cookie closer. Wren did too. They shared their last cookies. The mouse’s eyes got wide. It looked happy. It made a happy squeak, like a little bell. It took a nibble from each cookie.

The three friends shared in the soft moonlight. The mouse ate slowly. It tasted so good.

Soon, the mouse had a full tummy. It said thank you. It ran off into the soft grass to its cozy home.

Cherry and Wren watched the stars twinkle. They felt warm and safe. No cookies were left, but the window still held moonlight, and the moon flowers still nodded in the breeze.

Soon their eyes felt heavy. They were sleepy. They drifted into happy dreams.
